rim tube.notes: Converted from a per-length rate sheet, not quoted per metre. mwpbnp.com/pricing lists 'MS Pipe Prime Round' per 20 RFT by OD and SWG (e.g. 1" 18SWG Rs 1,458; 1-1/2" 18SWG Rs 2,228; 2-7/8" 16SWG Rs 5,936; 4" 16SWG Rs 7,807). Back-solving each row against pipe weight (mass/m = pi*t*(OD-t)*7850) gives a self-consistent Rs 320-340/kg for prime MS round tube at retail - the table is internally consistent to within 5%, which is why I trust it. A 40 mm OD x 2 mm wall tube weighs 1.874 kg/m, so material = Rs 505/m at a Rs 270/kg wholesale/local-quality rate up to Rs 675/m at Rs 360/kg (Quetta retail, +5-8% over Rawalpindi/Karachi for freight). ROLLING IS AN ESTIMATE, not a found price: no Pakistani shop publishes rolling rates (Peak Engineering lists 'plate bending & rolling' as a service but quotes only on request). R/D = 62 is a gentle curve needing no mandrel or sand-filling, so I allow Rs 150-450/m of rolling charge, typical ~Rs 250/m. Note 2 mm wall is 14 SWG, off the published table, so it is interpolated. Confidence: medium on material, low on the rolling component - get a real quote from a Brandreth Road / Shershah rolling shop before committing.
rim tube.check: mwpbnp.com/pricing opened and confirmed: MS Pipe Prime Round per 20 RFT, 1" 18SWG Rs 1,458, 1-1/2" 16SWG Rs 2,944, 2-7/8" 16SWG Rs 5,936, 4" 16SWG Rs 7,807 - all exactly as quoted. I back-solved three rows independently (1" 16SWG 0.953 kg/m -> Rs 333/kg; 2-7/8" 16SWG 2.862 kg/m -> Rs 340/kg; 4" 16SWG 4.009 kg/m -> Rs 319/kg), so the researcher's Rs 320-340/kg is real and self-consistent. His 40 mm OD x 2 mm = 1.874 kg/m is correct; at the observed Rs 330/kg that is Rs 618/m of material, so typical Rs 850 implies ~Rs 230 of rolling, which is a defensible allowance. Two caveats. post / mast.unit: per m (material + a share of erection hardware)

MEDIUM class 100 mm NB is OD 114.3 x 4.5 mm wall = 12.2 kg/m (BS 1387 nominal) - much heavier than EL. Black MS medium pipe from a local (non-branded) mill runs Rs 280-340/kg at the rates implied by the mwpbnp round-tube table, giving Rs 3,400-4,150/m; branded IIL medium in black would be ~Rs 5,600/m. zahidco shows GI Medium IIL starting at Rs 3,518 (that is the 1/2" entry) and builddurable lists IIL GI(M) at Rs 9,203.82 per nali without stating the size, so neither pins 4" medium directly - I extrapolated by weight. Erection-hardware share: 300x300x12 base plate (~8.5 kg, Rs ~2,800), four M16 anchor bolts (Rs 1,600-3,600), gussets and primer (Rs ~3,000) = Rs 7,400-9,400, spread over a 4-6 m mast = Rs 700-2,000/m. arm carrying F.notes: '60 mm (2 inch)' is ambiguous in the Pakistani market, so I priced the band. 60 mm OD x 2 mm tube = 2.86 kg/m -> Rs 800-1,030/m at Rs 280-360/kg (rate back-solved from the mwpbnp per-20-RFT round-tube table, whose 2-7/8" 16SWG row = Rs 974/m for a 2.87 kg/m section - almost exactly this weight, so the low end is a near-direct read). 2" NB LIGHT pipe (60.3 x 2.9 mm, 4.11 kg/m) = Rs 1,150-1,480/m; 2" NB MEDIUM (60.3 x 3.6 mm, 5.03 kg/m) = Rs 1,400-1,800/m. By weight: 50 mm OD x 2.0 mm = 2.37 kg/m -> Rs 660-850/m; x 2.5 mm = 2.93 kg/m -> Rs 820-1,050/m; x 3.2 mm = 3.68 kg/m -> Rs 1,030-1,320/m, all at Rs 280-360/kg. Typical assumes a 2-2.5 mm wall. His typical of Rs 900 sits inside that for the 2-2.5 mm wall he states. A 2.0 mm wall (heavier than 16 SWG) works out to ~1.13 kg/m = Rs 360-410/m at the implied Rs 320-360/kg. LOW = 20 SWG thin-wall, TYPICAL = 18 SWG, HIGH = 2 mm wall plus a Quetta freight margin. Quoted rates are for prime tube; 'commercial'/second-quality tube in the bazaar is 10-15% cheaper. Confidence high.
A-frames.check: The cleanest line in the table, and it verifies exactly. mwpbnp 1" MS prime round per 20 RFT (6.096 m): 20SWG Rs 1,105 = Rs 181.3/m, 19SWG Rs 1,216 = Rs 199.5/m, 18SWG Rs 1,458 = Rs 239.2/m, 16SWG Rs 1,937 = Rs 317.8/m. Every one of his per-metre figures reproduces to the rupee. Typical Rs 290 sits correctly between 18 and 16 SWG. High confidence is justified.

arc rail.notes: Material is the same 25 mm tube as the A-frames: Rs 190-430/m from the mwpbnp per-20-RFT table (1" 20SWG Rs 181/m to 2 mm wall Rs ~410/m). ROLLING IS AN ESTIMATE - I could not find any published Pakistani pipe-rolling rate despite several searches; Peak Engineering advertises rolling but quotes only on request, and no bazaar shop publishes a rate card. A 4.35 m radius on 25 mm tube is R/D = 174, an extremely gentle curve, so I allow Rs 120-400/m, typical ~Rs 280/m, which includes the shop's per-piece setup amortised over a few metres. Short single pieces will be charged per-piece (expect a Rs 1,500-3,000 minimum per visit regardless of length), so the per-metre figure only holds if you roll several rails at once. Widen this if you need a tight tolerance on the radius. Confidence low on rolling, medium-high on material.
arc rail.check: Material half verifies against the same confirmed 1" rows as the A-frames line, and is internally consistent with it. The rolling half is unsourced and I confirmed independently that it cannot be sourced: peak.com.pk publishes no rates (quote-on-request only, verified by fetch), and a fresh search for pipe/section rolling charges anywhere in Pakistan returned nothing usable. So Rs 570 typical is material (verified) plus an unverifiable Rs 280 allowance. The researcher's own warning is the operative one and I would repeat it louder: a rolling shop charges per setup, so a Rs 1,500-3,000 minimum per visit can double or triple the effective per-metre cost if you roll only one or two short rails. Number left alone for want of anything better.

bearings.notes: Read live off Daraz.pk. One Punjab seller lists a consistent UCP ladder: UCP210 Rs 2,300, UCP211 Rs 2,700, UCP212 Rs 3,000, UCP213 Rs 3,550, UCP214 Rs 4,200. The UCP204-206 sizes did not appear in that seller's listings on the day I looked, so I extrapolated the ladder downward: UCP204 ~Rs 1,200-1,500, UCP205 ~Rs 1,400-1,600, UCP206 ~Rs 1,600-1,900. Corroborating points actually seen: a WGD UC204 insert bearing at Rs 1,499 (Daraz, Sindh), a KBCC UC206 at Rs 1,999 and a 'UC Bearing' at Rs 1,010 (both OLX). counterweight.notes: Three very different routes, hence the wide band. (1) CONCRETE cast on site in a welded steel skirt: ~0.022 m3 for 50 kg, so Rs 400-700 of cement/sand/aggregate plus a light steel frame and lifting eye plus a fraction of a mason-day (Quetta mason Rs 1,600-2,000/day per concretesmath) = Rs 2,000-4,000. This is the low end and the sane choice. (2) SCRAP STEEL plate or billet offcuts welded into a block: Karachi iron scrap was Rs 35.34/kg mixed and Rs 41-42/kg for HMS 1 on 6 Sep 2026 (getscraprate); a Quetta scrap dealer will charge more for clean cut plate, call it Rs 60-120/kg = Rs 3,000-7,000 for 50 kg plus welding. (3) NEW CAST IRON from a foundry at roughly Rs 300-450/kg = Rs 15,000-27,000 - that is the high end. I deliberately excluded gym weight plates: Daraz shows a 10 kg iron dumbbell set at Rs 6,999 (~Rs 700/kg), which would be Rs 35,000 for 50 kg and is the worst way to buy dead weight. Confidence medium on the concrete and scrap routes, low on the cast-iron foundry rate (that one is inferred from general foundry practice, not a quote I found).

lid.notes: Converted from per-sheet to per-piece. A 0.9 m disc is 0.636 m2: 15.0 kg at 3 mm, 10.0 kg at 2 mm. mwpbnp's MS sheet table gives 16 SWG (1.63 mm) 4'x4' at Rs 4,992, i.e. Rs 3,360/m2 or Rs ~263/kg; 2-3 mm plate typically trades at Rs 250-310/kg (cross-check: raweasycorp quoted HRC at Rs 195,000/ton = Rs 195/kg ex-Moin Steel Market Karachi on 20 Aug 2026, so Rs 250-310/kg retail for cut plate is a normal margin). Material is therefore Rs 2,500-4,600. But you cannot buy a disc - a 4'x4' 3 mm sheet is ~35 kg and the disc uses 43% of it, so either you pay Rs 9,000+ for the sheet and keep the offcut, or the fabricator sells you the disc at Rs 300-350/kg including cutting = Rs 4,500-5,300. Add gas cutting, an edge stiffening ring or rolled lip, a welded handle, hinge or lifting lug, and primer/heat paint: roughly half a fabricator-day at the Quetta welder+helper rate of Rs 2,800-3,800 = Rs 1,500-2,500, plus consumables. HIGH covers 3 mm plate, a proper rolled rim, insulation backing and a Karachi shop rate. Confidence medium.

His own build-up (Rs 4,500-5,300 for the cut disc + Rs 1,500-2,500 labour + consumables) totals ~Rs 6,500-8,000 against a stated typical of Rs 9,000 - about 15% of unexplained headroom, presumably the stiffening ring and paint. strip bearing.notes: Assembled from real Daraz/OLX component prices read live. Deep-groove ball bearings: 6202 (15x35x11) Rs 120, 6201 Rs 600, no.609 Rs 380, NSK-china 6201-6208 from Rs 375, NTN 6301 Rs 715, NTN 6304 Rs 1,130, NTN 6004 Rs 1,265 (Daraz); OLX shows NTN 6301 at Rs 1,299 and 6304 at Rs 2,000. Shaft couplings: an aluminium rigid flange motor shaft coupler is Rs 835 (Daraz). Ready-made small mounted units: KFL08 flange block Rs 470, KP08 pillow block Rs 550, a 2-pack KP08 Rs 1,300. LOW = one Chinese 6202 plus a set-screw collar, bought in the bazaar. TYPICAL = two bearings, a rigid coupling and a small welded/turned bracket. HIGH = NTN/NSK bearings plus a properly machined housing (lathe time in Quetta or Karachi is Rs 1,500-4,000 for a small part). Confidence medium; the exact figure depends entirely on whether the housing is machined or improvised.

They are all in the right range for Chinese and NTN bearings sold in Pakistan, and the assembly logic (two bearings + rigid coupling + small bracket = Rs 2,200) is sound, so I have no basis to move the number. The researcher's own caveat is the important one and I agree with it: the figure is dominated by whether the housing is machined or improvised, and the Rs 700-5,000 spread honestly reflects that. Re-cite as product pages before this goes in a budget.

fabrication.notes: Direct read from a 2026 city-by-city daily-wage table. Welder/fabricator (skilled): QUETTA Rs 2,000-2,800/day, Karachi Rs 3,000-4,000, Lahore Rs 2,500-3,500, Islamabad Rs 3,200-4,500, Peshawar Rs 2,200-3,000. Helper/mazdoor (unskilled): QUETTA Rs 800-1,000/day, Karachi Rs 1,200-1,500. So welder-with-helper is Rs 2,800-3,800/day in Quetta and Rs 4,200-5,500/day in Karachi - those are the bare wage numbers and they are the LOW end. HIGH of Rs 9,000 covers hiring a WORKSHOP rather than two men: the shop rate bundles the welding set, grinder, cutting gas, electrodes, power (a real cost given Quetta load-shedding, often a generator) and the shop's margin, which in practice runs Rs 6,000-10,000/day - that uplift is my inference, not a published figure. The source itself calls its numbers 'indicative mid-point daily wages for 2026' to be verified locally. Confidence medium-high on the wages, medium on the shop-rate uplift.
